subject: geography
title: River Processes and Floods
welcome_lead: From mountain torrents to lowland meanders, follow rivers as they shape land and threaten communities.
meta_desc: Geography Adventure: river processes, landforms and flood management.
final_note: You have studied a river's life — and the floods that humans must live with. Hard and soft engineering must be balanced.

concepts.def: Wearing away of channel bed and banks by hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition and corrosion.
Movement of sediment by traction, saltation, suspension and solution.
Settling of sediment when river energy falls, forming features like floodplains and deltas.
Sinuous river bend formed by lateral erosion on the outer bank and deposition on the inner bank.
Built structures such as dams, levees and channel straightening for flood defence.
Non-structural approaches like floodplain zoning, afforestation and wetland restoration.

walkthroughs.body_html: Upper-course rivers tend to vertical erosion, forming V-shaped valleys, waterfalls and rapids. Middle-course rivers develop meanders through helicoidal flow and lateral erosion. Lower-course rivers create wide floodplains and deposit deltas where they meet still water.

Floods may be flash (rapid onset) or seasonal (monsoon, snowmelt). Causes include intense or prolonged rainfall, deforestation, urbanisation reducing infiltration, dam failure and sea-level rise at estuaries. Climate change is intensifying both extremes.

The Three Gorges Dam on the Yangtze illustrates large-scale hard engineering for flood control and hydroelectricity, but at social and ecological cost. The Room for the River programme in the Netherlands and Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SuDS) demonstrate softer approaches embracing controlled flooding and ecosystem services.
